parts:
Hi,

I've been recently experimenting with choiceRT_lba function and tried to fit it to my dataset. Unfortunately, the model returns biased estimates and doesn't seem to sample the posterior space efficiently for some reason. 

DATASET:
- 23 participants
- 3 conditions
 - trials per condition: 128 (cond 1), 64 (cond 2 & 3)
- 2AFC

MODEL GROUP ESTIMATES:
               mean se_mean    sd     2.5%      25%      50%      75%    97.5% n_eff Rhat
mu_d             1.73    0.01  0.22     1.24     1.61     1.75     1.87     2.06  1516    1
mu_A             0.98    0.01  0.39     0.12     0.72     1.05     1.28     1.58  1660    1
mu_v[1,1]        3.88    0.00  0.14     3.62     3.79     3.88     3.97     4.16  2482    1
mu_v[1,2]        2.89    0.00  0.14     2.61     2.79     2.89     2.98     3.17  4724    1
mu_v[2,1]        3.17    0.00  0.11     2.96     3.10     3.17     3.25     3.39  2826    1
mu_v[2,2]        2.23    0.00  0.13     1.98     2.15     2.23     2.31     2.47  4066    1
mu_v[3,1]        2.87    0.00  0.11     2.66     2.79     2.87     2.94     3.08  3395    1
mu_v[3,2]        2.09    0.00  0.10     1.90     2.02     2.09     2.15     2.29  3207    1
mu_tau           0.03    0.00  0.02     0.00     0.01     0.02     0.04     0.09  2705    1
sigma_d          0.58    0.00  0.17     0.37     0.47     0.55     0.66     1.02  2161    1
sigma_A          0.82    0.00  0.26     0.44     0.62     0.77     0.97     1.42  3645    1

Notice the non-decision time estimate: it is impossibly short. Other parameters seem reasonable.

WARNINGS
Warning messages:
1: There were 653 divergent transitions after warmup. Increasing adapt_delta above 0.95 may help. See
http://mc-stan.org/misc/warnings.html#divergent-transitions-after-warmup 
2: There were 2 transitions after warmup that exceeded the maximum treedepth. Increase max_treedepth above 10. See
http://mc-stan.org/misc/warnings.html#maximum-treedepth-exceeded 
3: There were 2 chains where the estimated Bayesian Fraction of Missing Information was low. See
http://mc-stan.org/misc/warnings.html#bfmi-low 

As you can see, the problem must be connected to the absurd amount of divergent transitions. I don't believe that simply increasing the adopt_alpha will be enough to correct for this. 

SIMULATION
To check whether this is a dataset issue, I've run a simulation with similar parameters with same number of participants and trial per condition to see whether the model can recreate them:

 #set true params
v1=rnorm(23,4.0,.2) # vector for drift rate accumulator 1
v2=rnorm(23,3.0,.2)
v1c2=rnorm(23,3.0,.2)
v2c2=rnorm(23,2.0,.2)
v1c3= rnorm(23,2.5,.2 )
v2c3 = rnorm(23,1.5,.2)
b = rnorm(23,2,.3)
A = rnorm(23,1,.3)
s = 1
t0 =rnorm(23,.4,.1)

#simulate data
simDatC1 = vector(mode='list',length(23))
simDatC2 = vector(mode='list',length(23))
simDatC3 = vector(mode='list',length(23))
for (i in 1:23) {
  simDatC1[[i]] <- rlba(n=128,A = A[i], b = b[i], t0 = t0[i], s = 1, v = c(v1[i],v2[i]))

  simDatC3[[i]] <- rlba(n=64,A = A[i], b = b[i], t0 = t0[i], s = 1, v = c(v1c3[i],v2c3[i]))
}

simDatC1 = do.call('rbind',simDatC1)
simDatC2 = do.call('rbind',simDatC2)
simDatC3 = do.call('rbind',simDatC3)
simDat = rbind(simDatC1,simDatC2,simDatC3)
names(simDat) <- c('choice', 'RT')
simDat$condition = c(rep(1,dim(simDatC1)[1]),rep(2, dim(simDatC2)[1]), rep(3, dim(simDatC3)[1]))
simDat$subjID = c(rep(1:23,each=128),rep(1:23,each=64),rep(1:23,each=64))
write.table(simDat, 'simDat.txt',row.names = F)

#model
simLBA = choiceRT_lba(nwarmup=2500,niter=5000)

mu_v[2,1]      2.91    0.02  0.09   2.73   2.85   2.91   2.98   3.10    18 1.09
mu_v[2,2]      1.95    0.02  0.08   1.80   1.90   1.95   2.01   2.11    15 1.14
mu_v[3,1]      2.36    0.02  0.08   2.20   2.30   2.36   2.42   2.53    18 1.08
mu_v[3,2]      1.36    0.02  0.10   1.18   1.29   1.36   1.43   1.55    22 1.07

sigma_A        0.26    0.01  0.07   0.15   0.21   0.25   0.29   0.42   157 1.01

As you can see, the estimates here seem more reasonable and close to the true values. However ,there were still some problems during sampling:

Warning messages:
1: There were 19 divergent transitions after warmup. Increasing adapt_delta above 0.95 may help. See
http://mc-stan.org/misc/warnings.html#divergent-transitions-after-warmup 
2: There were 2483 transitions after warmup that exceeded the maximum treedepth. Increase max_treedepth above 10. See
http://mc-stan.org/misc/warnings.html#maximum-treedepth-exceeded 
3: There were 1 chains where the estimated Bayesian Fraction of Missing Information was low. See

The amount of divergent transitions is smaller, however this time the treedepth seems to be a bigger issue.

CONCLUSIONS:
The model for some reason cannot accommodate my data. The fit for the simulation looks much better and, unlike in the case of my data, seem to be easily adjusted by increasing adapt_alpha and treedepth params. 

I am kind of stuck, and not sure what to do next. One suggested solution on STAN forums for divergent transitions is to reparametrize the model, which I a) am unable to do, due to lack of required mathematical background b) am unsure whether it would be helpful. Is it possible that LBA is somehow unable to accommodate my dataset? If so, why might that be?

Best,
Wojciech

Hi Nate,

Thanks for a quick response.

1. Sure. Attached is the traceplot, along with 2 others.

2. That is because the diagnostic plots (pairs) show divergent transitions scattered all over the place, as opposed to above the diagonal, what would suggest insufficient adopt_alpha (http://mc-stan.org/misc/warnings.html).  Also, the sheer number of them suggests that something else had to go wrong.

 Just to verify this, I tried running a model with adopt_alpha=0.99, but after 4 days of estimation my computer crashed.

3. I'm using seconds.Same basic summary stats:

  cond        RT          pref
1   EE  0.7964920    0.7223769
2   HH   0.6454690   0.7247455
3   TT   0.8662433   0.7048455

'cond' is the condition
'pref' is preference for 1 option over other, which can be treated similarly to accuracy, as long as the model is concerned

The pairs plots can reveal if there are any trade-offs between parameters, but it looks like there are not any according to these images. Also, the divergences (red dots) appear to be randomly distributed throughout the parameter space, so I do not think they are a major concern. If they were specific to a certain area of the parameter space (see Neil's Funnel: https://betanalpha.github.io/assets/case_studies/divergences_and_bias.html), then we may want to re-parameterize the model. 


It may be beneficial to try setting the lower bound of the starting point (A) parameter to be > non-decision time (tau). This could be accomplished by manipulating the truncated priors on the group- and individual- level parameters like so: 


model {
  // Hyperparameter means
  mu_tau ~ normal(.2,.5)T[0,];
  mu_d   ~ normal(.5,1)T[0,];
  mu_A   ~ normal(.5,1)T[mu_tau,];
  
  // Hyperparameter sigmas
  sigma_d   ~ gamma(1,1);
  sigma_A   ~ gamma(1,1);
  sigma_tau ~ gamma(1,1);
  
  // Hyperparameter means and sigmas for multiple drift rates
  for(j in 1:N_cond) {
    for(n in 1:N_choices) {
      mu_v[j,n]    ~ normal(2,1)T[0,];
      sigma_v[j,n] ~ gamma(1,1);
    }
  }
     
  for(i in 1:N) {
    // Declare variables
    int n_trials;
    
    // Individual parameters
    tau[i] ~ normal(mu_tau, sigma_tau)T[0,];
    d[i]   ~ normal(mu_d, sigma_d)T[0,];
    A[i]   ~ normal(mu_A, sigma_A)T[tau[i],];
    
    for(j in 1:N_cond) {
      // Store number of trials for subject/condition pair
      n_trials = N_tr_cond[i,j];
      
      for(n in 1:N_choices){
        // Drift rate is normally distributed
        v[i,j,n] ~ normal(mu_v[j,n], sigma_v[j,n])T[0,];
      }
      // Likelihood of RT x Choice
      RT[i,j,,1:n_trials] ~ lba(d[i], A[i], v[i,j,], s, tau[i]);
    }
  }
}

One thing to note—it could be that you are getting these results because participants have a decision in mind before the stimuli are presented. The pairs plots can reveal if there are any trade-offs between parameters, but it looks like there are not any according to these images. Also, the divergences (red dots) appear to be randomly distributed throughout the parameter space, so I do not think they are a major concern. If they were specific to a certain area of the parameter space (see Neil's Funnel: https://betanalpha.github.io/assets/case_studies/divergences_and_bias.html), then we may want to re-parameterize the model. 


It may be beneficial to try setting the lower bound of the starting point (A) parameter to be > non-decision time (tau). This could be accomplished by manipulating the truncated priors on the group- and individual- level parameters like so: 


model {
  // Hyperparameter means
  mu_tau ~ normal(.2,.5)T[0,];
  mu_d   ~ normal(.5,1)T[0,];
  mu_A   ~ normal(.5,1)T[mu_tau,];
  
  // Hyperparameter sigmas
  sigma_d   ~ gamma(1,1);
  sigma_A   ~ gamma(1,1);
  sigma_tau ~ gamma(1,1);
  
  // Hyperparameter means and sigmas for multiple drift rates
  for(j in 1:N_cond) {
    for(n in 1:N_choices) {
      mu_v[j,n]    ~ normal(2,1)T[0,];
      sigma_v[j,n] ~ gamma(1,1);
    }
  }
     
  for(i in 1:N) {
    // Declare variables
    int n_trials;
    
    // Individual parameters
    tau[i] ~ normal(mu_tau, sigma_tau)T[0,];
    d[i]   ~ normal(mu_d, sigma_d)T[0,];
    A[i]   ~ normal(mu_A, sigma_A)T[tau[i],];
    
    for(j in 1:N_cond) {
      // Store number of trials for subject/condition pair
      n_trials = N_tr_cond[i,j];
      
      for(n in 1:N_choices){
        // Drift rate is normally distributed
        v[i,j,n] ~ normal(mu_v[j,n], sigma_v[j,n])T[0,];
      }
      // Likelihood of RT x Choice
      RT[i,j,,1:n_trials] ~ lba(d[i], A[i], v[i,j,], s, tau[i]);
    }
  }
}

I bolded the sections that I changed. This will just make sure that tau is lower than A. I have not tried this particular parameterization, but the syntax is all correct.

It may be beneficial to try setting the lower bound of the starting point (A) parameter to be > non-decision time (tau). This could be accomplished by manipulating the truncated priors on the group- and individual- level parameters like so: 


model {

  mu_d   ~ normal(.5,1)T[0,];
  mu_A   ~ normal(.5,1)T[mu_tau,];
  
  // Hyperparameter sigmas
  sigma_d   ~ gamma(1,1);
  sigma_A   ~ gamma(1,1);
  sigma_tau ~ gamma(1,1);
  
  // Hyperparameter means and sigmas for multiple drift rates
  for(j in 1:N_cond) {
    for(n in 1:N_choices) {
      mu_v[j,n]    ~ normal(2,1)T[0,];
      sigma_v[j,n] ~ gamma(1,1);
    }
  }
     
  for(i in 1:N) {
    // Declare variables
    int n_trials;
    
    // Individual parameters
    tau[i] ~ normal(mu_tau, sigma_tau)T[0,];
    d[i]   ~ normal(mu_d, sigma_d)T[0,];
    A[i]   ~ normal(mu_A, sigma_A)T[tau[i],];
    
    for(j in 1:N_cond) {
      // Store number of trials for subject/condition pair
      n_trials = N_tr_cond[i,j];

      // Likelihood of RT x Choice

  mu_d   ~ normal(.5,1)T[0,];
  mu_A   ~ normal(.5,1)T[mu_tau,];

  sigma_A   ~ gamma(1,1);

  for(i in 1:N) {
    // Declare variables

    d[i]   ~ normal(mu_d, sigma_d)T[0,];
